mainTopic: Holy-to-holy מעילה, who is included, and the three comparisons that set when using הקדש requires damage
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about מעילה, misusing הקדש property. A person commits מעילה even when he moves holy money to another holy use for his own benefit, such as paying for his own bird offerings, שקל, חטאת or אשם. רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה argue about when that liability starts, and 'תמעל מעל' is the source. The גמרא explains why the ברייתא had to include the king and the כהן גדול: we might have thought they are not a 'זר' to the anointing oil. Next, the גמרא lists three comparisons the Torah makes for מעילה. From סוטה we learn there can be liability without damage, from עבודה זרה that an item which can be damaged must actually be damaged, and from תרומה that damaging without benefit is פטור. רב כהנא then asks whether gold really cannot be damaged, and רב זביד gives two answers. Finally, רב פפא explains that the משנה's חטאת that needs real damage is a blemished animal, whose value drops when its wool is taken.

steps.title: The mistaken assumption: liability only when holy becomes ordinary
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its 'one might have thought' idea: maybe a person only commits מעילה when the item leaves holy status and becomes חול.
steps.simpleTranslation: …until it goes out from holy to ordinary.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the ברייתא in the middle. It is finishing a 'one might think' idea: a person might only be liable for מעילה once the holy item becomes ordinary (חול), just like a non-כהן who eats תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison is to תרומה: a non-כהן eats it and turns it into his own private food, moving it from קודש to חול. The assumption is that מעילה works the same way. This sets up the next line, which will show that moving from holy to holy also counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy or sacred status or property
Ordinary, non-sacred status
Until it goes out of one status into another

phrases.english: – until it goes out from the sacred to the non-sacred.
phrases.notes: This ends a 'you might have thought' line. Like a non-כהן eating תרומה, liability would only start when the item becomes ordinary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous daf, finishing its 'one might think' idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הוה אמינא: מעילה requires the item to go from קודש to חול.

steps.title: Moving from holy to holy also counts, says רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that using הקדש money for one's own holy obligations, like bird offerings, the שקל, or a חטאת or אשם, is also מעילה. According to רבי שמעון, the person is liable as soon as he spends the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: From holy to holy also counts. For example, he used הקדש money to buy the bird offerings of a זב, a זבה, or a woman after childbirth, or paid his half-shekel, or brought his own חטאת and אשם from הקדש. Once he spent the money, he committed מעילה. This is רבי שמעון's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the assumption from step 1. Even when holy money stays holy, a person who uses it for his own personal obligations commits מעילה. רבי שמעון says this happens the moment he spends the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money never becomes ordinary, because it buys קרבנות. But these קרבנות are the person's own duty and should be paid from his private money, so he gains personally from הקדש. For רבי שמעון, that gain happens right away when he pays.

keyTerms.meaning: Pairs of birds (doves or pigeons) brought as קרבנות
Men or women with a certain bodily discharge who must bring bird offerings
Women after childbirth, who bring a bird offering
Property belonging to the בית המקדש
He committed מעילה, meaning he misused holy property

steps.confusionAlert: The money is not being used for something ordinary; it buys real קרבנות. The מעילה is that he used holy money to pay his own personal debt to Heaven.

phrases.english: From the sacred to the sacred, such as:
he bought the bird pairs of zavim,
phrases.notes: He paid for them with הקדש money. See ויקרא 15:14.

phrases.english: and the bird pairs of zavot, and the bird pairs of women after childbirth,
or paid his shekel,
or brought his sin offering and his guilt offering from consecrated property –
once he spent it, he committed misuse,
these are the words of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns the assumption of step 1 by showing that holy-to-holy use is also מעילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using הקדש funds for one's own קרבן obligations is מעילה; according to רבי שמעון, liability starts as soon as the money is spent.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only once the blood is sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees about timing. The person is not liable until the blood of the korban is sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: not until the blood is sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different moment for when the מעילה happens: only when the כהן sprinkles the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages agree that this is מעילה; they argue only about when it happens. For רבי יהודה, the real benefit is the כפרה, which comes through sprinkling the blood, so that is when he has actually gained from הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the קרבן's blood on the מזבח, the step that brings כפרה
Atonement

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
not until he sprinkles the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהודה אומר עד שיזרוק הדם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רבי שמעון about the timing of liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the מעילה happens only at the sprinkling of the blood.

steps.title: The source: 'תמעל מעל' means in any case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks where we learn that holy-to-holy use is מעילה, and answers from the doubled words 'תמעל מעל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? The פסוק says 'תמעל מעל', meaning in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the source for the whole idea that holy-to-holy use is also מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubled wording 'תמעל מעל' is read as widening the law: מעילה applies in any case. So it is not limited to moving holy property into ordinary use, which closes off the idea from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches', the opening of a proof from a verse
'Commits a misuse', doubled wording used to include more cases
In any case, with no exceptions

steps.whatToRemember: מעילה is not only turning holy property into ordinary property. Using holy funds for your own holy obligations also counts, based on 'תמעל מעל'. רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה argue only about when the liability starts.

phrases.english: From where do we know this? The verse teaches:
"commits a misuse" – in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule taught in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That holy-to-holy use of הקדש for personal benefit is מעילה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The doubled wording 'תמעל מעל' in ויקרא 5:15, read as 'in any case'.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the start of the ברייתא: everyone is included
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the beginning of the ברייתא, which said 'נפש' includes an ordinary person, the נשיא, and the כהן משוח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'נפש' includes an ordinary individual, the king, and the anointed כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the start of the ברייתא so that it can ask a question about it. This step sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learned from the word 'נפש' that every kind of person is included in מעילה, even the king and the כהן גדול. The גמרא is about to ask why this needed to be said at all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A soul', meaning any person
An ordinary individual
The king or ruler
The anointed כהן גדול
Included in the meaning of the word

phrases.english: The Master said: "Anyone" –
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the opening of this same ברייתא. The word is from ויקרא 5:15.

phrases.english: both the individual and the king
and the anointed priest are included in the meaning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר מר נפש אחד היחיד ואחד הנשיא ואחד המשוח במשמע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the timing dispute and goes back to analyze the opening line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone, including the נשיא and the כהן משוח, is included in מעילה through the word 'נפש'.

steps.title: Why say it? 'נפש' obviously means anyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: what would we have thought otherwise? 'נפש' already plainly includes everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: What might we have thought? It is obvious, since 'נפש' is written!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to point out that the king and the כהן גדול are included. The word 'נפש' already means any person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא should not teach something that needs no teaching. If 'נפש' plainly covers everyone, the ברייתא's statement seems unnecessary. So the גמרא wants to know what wrong idea it was trying to block.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For one might have thought', a mistaken idea the ברייתא is blocking
'It is obvious', a challenge that something didn't need saying
It is written in the פסוק

phrases.english: "For one might have thought" – what?
It is obvious – "anyone" is written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that 'נפש' includes the יחיד, the נשיא, and the משוח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'נפש' plainly means any person, so spelling out that the king and the כהן גדול are included seems unnecessary. What mistaken idea was being prevented?

steps.title: We might have thought the anointed ones are not 'strangers'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא had to include the כהן משוח and the king. Otherwise we might think they are exempt, since the Torah calls the one who misuses the anointing oil a זר, and they were anointed with that oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: the Torah says 'whoever puts any of it on a stranger.' This man is not a stranger, since he was anointed with it. So the ברייתא teaches us that he is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6: why did the ברייתא need to say that נפש includes the נשיא and the כהן משוח?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was a real reason to think these two people are left out. The Torah speaks of putting the anointing oil on a זר, a stranger, and the כהן גדול and the king are not strangers to that oil, because they were anointed with it. The ברייתא teaches that they are still fully included in מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Lest you say.' This introduces a wrong idea that the teaching comes to block.
'The Merciful One.' This is how the גמרא refers to ה׳, as the One who gave the Torah.
A 'stranger,' meaning an outsider who is not part of the special group.
The holy anointing oil, used to anoint the כהן גדול and kings.
'It teaches us.' This shows that the teaching is needed after all.

phrases.english: Lest you say
the Merciful One said
"or whoever puts any of it upon a stranger"
phrases.notes: שמות 30:33. This verse is about the holy anointing oil.

phrases.english: and this one is not a "stranger"
since he was anointed with it
phrases.notes: 'He' means the כהן גדול or the king. Both were anointed with this oil.

phrases.english: it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 6 by showing that the ברייתא's teaching was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: it shows a mistaken idea that the teaching comes to block.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן משוח and the king are not a זר to the anointing oil, so they might be outside the laws of מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: נפש includes them too. They are liable for מעילה like everyone else.

steps.title: Three comparisons, starting with סוטה: liable even without damage
steps.stepSummary: The Torah compared מעילה to סוטה, עבודה זרה, and תרומה. The comparison to סוטה teaches that you can be liable even without damaging the item. For example, a woman who puts a הקדש ring on her finger has committed מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah compared מעילה to a סוטה, to idol worship, and to תרומה. It compared it to a סוטה: just as there she is guilty even though she caused no damage, with הקדש too, if a woman put a ring on her hand, she has committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a summary of three comparisons the Torah makes for מעילה, and explains the first one, סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מעל appears in the Torah's discussion of a סוטה as well. A סוטה is guilty even though her act left no physical mark. In the same way, using a הקדש item can be מעילה even when the item is not harmed at all, like wearing a ring.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He compared it.' The Torah links two topics so that one teaches about the other.
A married woman suspected of being unfaithful to her husband.
Damaged, or lowered in value.
A ring.

phrases.english: And the Merciful One compared it
phrases.notes: 'It' means מעילה. Each of the three comparisons that follow comes from a word these פסוקים share with מעילה.

phrases.english: to a sota, and to idol worship, and to teruma.

phrases.aramaic: לְסוֹטָה, דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא פָּגַם
phrases.english: To a sota: that even though there was no damage,
regarding consecrated property too,
if she put a ring on her hand, she has committed misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַקְּשַׁהּ רַחֲמָנָא לְסוֹטָה, וְלַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְלִתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of who is included and starts a summary of the basic rules of מעילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of the comparison to סוטה, there can be מעילה without any damage, as when a woman wears a הקדש ring.

steps.title: The עבודה זרה comparison: a damageable item needs a real change
steps.stepSummary: The comparison to עבודה זרה teaches that there must be a change. With a הקדש item that can be damaged, there is no מעילה until it is actually damaged, for example by chopping with a הקדש ax until the ax loses value.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the Torah compared it to idol worship, the lesson is that there is no liability until there is a change. With הקדש too, there is no liability until he chops with an ax and the ax becomes damaged, and it is actually damaged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second comparison, to עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Idol worship involves a change: a person switches from serving ה׳ to serving idols. In the same way, for a הקדש item that can be damaged, using it is not enough. The use must actually damage the item, like an ax that gets worn down from chopping.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship.
A change.
An ax.
'It will become damaged, and it is damaged.' The item must actually lose value through the use.

steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict the ring case in step 8. The ring cannot really be harmed by wearing it, so no damage is needed. The ax can be damaged, so for the ax there is no מעילה until it actually is damaged.

phrases.english: When the Merciful One compared it to idol worship,
it teaches that there is no liability until there is a change in it.
Regarding consecrated property too,
there is no liability until he chops with an ax
phrases.notes: This is a הקדש ax used to chop his own wood.

phrases.english: and it becomes damaged, and it is actually damaged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second of the three comparisons listed in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a הקדש item that can be damaged, there is no מעילה until the use actually damages it.

steps.title: The תרומה comparison: damaging without benefit is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The comparison to תרומה teaches that only eating counts, not destroying. So someone who damages an edible הקדש item without benefiting from it is פטור from מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah compared it to תרומה. Just as with תרומה the verse says 'if he eats,' which leaves out someone who only damages it, with הקדש too: any edible item, if he damages it, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third comparison, to תרומה, and so finishes the list of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about תרומה says 'if a man eats.' That leaves out someone who only destroys it, for example by spilling it. The same rule carries over to הקדש: damaging an edible item without getting any benefit from it is not מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן. Only כהנים may eat it.
Someone who damages or destroys something.
Something edible.
Exempt, not liable.

steps.whatToRemember: The three comparisons each teach one rule for מעילה. From סוטה: liability can come even without damage (the ring). From עבודה זרה: an item that can be damaged must actually be damaged (the ax). From תרומה: damaging without any benefit is פטור.
steps.whyThisMatters: Together these three comparisons set the basic rules for when using הקדש counts as מעילה. The key ideas are benefit, damage, and change.

phrases.english: The Merciful One compared it to teruma.
Just as with teruma,
"if he eats" excludes one who damages it,
regarding consecrated property too,
with any edible item,
when he damages it, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third and final comparison listed in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damaging an edible הקדש item without benefiting from it is פטור from מעילה.

steps.title: Doesn't gold get damaged too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's example of a woman wearing a הקדש gold chain, and רב כהנא challenges the idea that gold cannot be damaged.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'How? If she put on a chain, etc.' רב כהנא said to רב זביד: Is gold really something that cannot be damaged? Where did all the gold of נון's daughter-in-law go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a gold chain, which counts as an item that cannot be damaged. רב כהנא challenges this by pointing out that gold does wear away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses gold as its example of a הקדש item where you can be liable for מעילה without damaging it. רב כהנא argues that gold can be damaged, because נון's daughter-in-law had a lot of gold and it disappeared over time. If gold can be damaged, the example seems to belong in the other category.

keyTerms.meaning: A chain or necklace worn around the neck
Gold
Something that can be damaged or lose value
His daughter-in-law

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two categories. Gold is the משנה's example of an item that is NOT damaged by use, so מעילה happens just by benefiting from it. רב כהנא is questioning whether gold really belongs there.

phrases.english: How? She placed a chain, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: a woman who puts a הקדש gold chain on her neck is liable even though the gold is not damaged.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא לְרַב זְבִיד:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said to Rav Zevid:
And is gold not something that can be damaged?
But the gold of Nun's daughter-in-law,
phrases.notes: נון was a rich man who gave his son's bride lots of gold jewelry, and it wore away over the years.

phrases.english: where did it go?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's example of an item that cannot be damaged, which matches the סוטה comparison in Step 8, and questions it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's assumption that gold is an item that cannot be damaged
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Real life shows that gold wears away, like the gold of נון's daughter-in-law, so gold can be damaged.

steps.title: That gold was treated carelessly
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד answers that נון's daughter-in-law's gold disappeared because she was careless with it, like רב כהנא's own daughters-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said to him: Maybe it was like the gold your daughters-in-law toss around.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד gives his first answer. The gold did not wear out from normal use. It was lost or damaged because it was handled carelessly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from נון's family is pushed aside. Gold that is thrown around and neglected can get lost or ruined, but that does not show that normal wearing damages it. So gold can still count as an item that is not damaged by use.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe
They throw or toss aside carelessly
Your daughters-in-law

phrases.english: He said to him:
Perhaps it is like the gold that your daughters-in-law toss aside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's challenge by weakening his proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the evidence: the loss came from carelessness, not from normal wear.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נון's daughter-in-law's lost gold shows that gold gets damaged by use.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her gold was lost because she was careless, so this proves nothing about normal use.

steps.title: Gold is not damaged right away
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד adds a second answer: gold does wear down eventually, but it is not damaged at the moment someone uses it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: True, gold is not damaged right away when someone benefits from it. But does that mean it never wears down at all?
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד gives a second answer. He admits that gold wears down over a long time, but says that is not what the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's category is about whether one act of use causes immediate damage. Gold only wears away slowly over many years, so wearing it once causes no damage you can notice. That is why it still counts as an item that is not damaged by use.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, introducing an extra answer
Granted, true that
Immediately, right away
Damage, loss of value

steps.whatToRemember: An item that is 'not damaged' means one act of use does not damage it right away. Slow wear over many years doesn't change that, so gold stays the משנה's example.

phrases.english: And furthermore: granted that there is not
a case of benefiting and damaging immediately,
is there never any damage at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: נְהִי דְּלָא אִיכָּא נֶהֱנָה וּפָגַם לְאַלְתַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, stronger answer to the same challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the category more exactly: what counts is immediate damage, not slow wear over time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since gold eventually wears down, it should count as an item that can be damaged.
steps.terutzMaskana: Gold is not damaged immediately by use, so it remains an item that cannot be damaged for מעילה.

steps.title: Isn't an unblemished animal like the gold cup?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about benefiting from a חטאת, which requires damage, and asks why, since an unblemished animal seems to be like a gold cup that cannot be damaged.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who benefits from a חטאת, etc.' Now, if this is about an unblemished animal, it is just like the gold cup!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another line of the משנה, which says that taking wool from a חטאת is only מעילה if it causes damage. It challenges this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unblemished animal is going to be brought as a קרבן. Removing some wool doesn't make it any less fit for the מזבח. So it should be like the gold cup, where there is מעילה even without damage, and the משנה's demand for damage seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering, one of the קדשי קדשים
Now, consider: opening a logical challenge
An animal without a blemish, fit to be offered
A gold cup, the משנה's example of a הקדש item that cannot be damaged

phrases.english: One who benefits from a sin offering, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: for example, taking wool from a living חטאת is מעילה only if it damages the animal by a פרוטה's worth.

phrases.english: Now, if it is about an unblemished animal,
that is the same as a gold cup!
phrases.notes: The animal can still be offered after the wool is taken, so it isn't really damaged, just like the cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי אִי בִּבְהֵמָה תְּמִימָה, הַיְינוּ כּוֹס שֶׁל זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the gold discussion and questions another case in the משנה, using the gold cup as the comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that benefiting from a חטאת by taking its wool needs actual damage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unblemished animal stays fit for the מזבח after its wool is taken, so it is like the gold cup that cannot be damaged. That should mean מעילה even without damage.

steps.title: The case is a blemished animal
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the משנה is talking about a blemished חטאת, which can lose value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We are dealing with an animal that has a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by narrowing the משנה's case to a blemished animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished animal cannot be offered, so הקדש will sell it. Taking its wool lowers the price it will get. So it really is an item that can be damaged, and that is why the משנה requires damage before there is מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a blemish, unfit to be offered
We are dealing with (this case)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's חטאת case is a blemished animal. It will be sold, so losing wool lowers its value. That makes it an item that can be damaged, and מעילה needs real damage.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the rule clearly: whether something counts as 'damaged' depends on whether its use for הקדש loses value, not just whether something was physically removed.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
We are dealing with a blemished animal.
phrases.notes: A blemished animal will be sold, and less wool means a lower price, so taking the wool really damages it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 14 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case to a blemished animal, which can lose value.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's חטאת is unblemished, so it is like a gold cup that cannot be damaged.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חטאת is blemished and will be sold. Taking its wool lowers its value, so actual damage is required.
